title: European audiences and traveling conditions
summary: He says he is a king in Europe and 'Panama Who?' at home; he found transport poor but hotels good.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Uh huh. What countries did you seem to like best over there and what countries did you seem to like the jazz music best?

Well, I was very much impressed with the way they accepted the type of jazz that I was playing in places like France or Switzerland and Holland and Belgium. We were very successful in these places -- and also, Spain.
And how was the audience response?
Oh, the audience response was -- I often say to my friends that in Europe I'm a king and in my own country, I'm Panama Who?
How are the conditions there for traveling and living for musicians?

Well, I mean, it wasn't too good for passenger me because I'd been used to riding in 44 Greyhound busses, and they had -- what they had was one of these Fiat trucks that they put some seats in, which they used to carry the instruments in one half of it and then in the other half, they used as a bus, and it was very uncomfortable traveling like that.
But as far as the hotels; I mean, the
accommodations in the hotels, there was only one time that I stayed at a hotel that I wasn't happy with. All the rest of them were very nice.
Did you play with any European bands over there?
No, I never played with any European bands -- always American musicians, all except Roland who was the bass player.
